title: Questions to Ask During an Initial Architect Consultation in Scarsdale
excerpt: Starting a home renovation or addition in Scarsdale? Knowing what to ask your architect upfront saves time, money, and headaches. Here's what every homeowner should cover in that first meeting.
content:
You've decided it's time to tackle that kitchen remodel, add a second story, or expand your primary suite. Now you need an architect. That first conversation is your chance to figure out if you're working with the right person and if they understand your vision. The questions you ask matter more than you might think.

A good initial consultation should feel like a real conversation, not a sales pitch. You're interviewing them as much as they're learning about your project. Here's what to cover when you sit down with a residential architect in Scarsdale.

Ask About Their Experience with Your Specific Project Type

Not every architect has done what you want to do. If you're planning a second-story addition, ask if they've completed similar work in Scarsdale homes. If it's a kitchen remodel or historic restoration, ask for examples. You want someone who knows how to handle your particular challenge, not someone taking a guess.

Find out if they've worked with Scarsdale's building department before. Every Westchester municipality has its own permit process and requirements. An architect who knows the local officials and the typical timeline will save you frustration down the road.

Understand Their Role and Process

This is where the difference between hiring just an architect versus working with a design-build firm in Westchester becomes clear. Some architects design and hand off to a contractor. Others, like House Architecture & Construction, have a principal who is both a licensed architect in New York and a licensed general contractor who manages every project personally. Ask how your architect will be involved once construction starts.

Ask what the design process looks like. How many rounds of revisions are included? When do you get drawings? How will they handle changes mid-project? Understanding their workflow prevents surprises later.

Talk About Permits, Timeline, and Your Budget

Ask how long they expect the design phase to take before permits are submitted. Ask what they need from you to get started. Do they want to visit your home, or will they work from photos initially?

Be clear about your budget and ask them to be honest about what's realistic. You don't need a cost estimate in the first meeting, but you should discuss whether your budget aligns with your vision. A good architect will tell you if you need to adjust one or the other.

Ask about their fee structure too. Do they charge hourly? A flat fee? A percentage of construction costs? Different architects work differently, and you should know upfront.

Make Sure You're a Good Fit

The best design comes from good communication. Ask them about their design philosophy. Look at their portfolio. Do you like what they've done before? Can they point to home additions in Westchester or renovations that match the style you're after?

Trust your gut. If you feel rushed, dismissed, or like they're not listening, they're probably not the right fit. You're about to spend months working closely with this person. It should feel like a partnership.
